title: Minimum Operations to Sort a Permutation
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n, representing a permutation of integers from 0 to n-1, determine the minimum number of operations needed to sort the array in ascending order using only reverse operations on the entire array or left rotations by one position.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n, representing a permutation of integers from 0 to n-1, determine the minimum number of operations needed to sort the array in ascending order using only reverse operations on the entire array or left rotations by one position. If sorting is impossible, return -1.
constraints: nums is a permutation of 0 through n-1.
An operation either reverses the whole array or rotates it left by one.
Return the fewest operations to sort ascending, or -1.
hints: Rotations and full reversal can only produce a cyclic ascending or cyclic descending order.
Locate zero and test both directions around the cycle.
For each valid orientation, compare direct rotations with two reversals plus rotations.
The dihedral orbit contains exactly these two orientations, so all other permutations are unreachable.
editorial: The dihedral orbit contains exactly these two orientations, so all other permutations are unreachable.

tests.explanation: Two full reversals/rotations can sort this reachable orientation.
